tweet_summary: Elon Musk says Chris Nolan 'desecrated' the Odyssey so he would be eligible for an Academy Award (implying diversity-casting was driven by Oscar inclusion standards).
why_note_decision: Pure opinion ('desecrated') plus a causal-attribution claim ('so that he would be eligible for an Academy Award') that is unfalsifiable (we can't read Nolan's mind). The factual backdrop: Academy Best Picture inclusion standards (in effect since 2024) require films to meet 2 of 4 standards — casting is one option, but films can also qualify via crew, leadership, or audience-development criteria. Oppenheimer (all-white cast) won Best Picture under these same rules. Variety, No Film School, and other outlets have noted Musk's framing is misleading — but the tweet itself doesn't make a falsifiable claim, it makes a snarky editorial assertion of motive. Original AI note tries to spell out the inclusion rules — got rated notHelpfulMissingKeyPoints (603), notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded (621). Opinion-bait from Musk is exactly the false-positive trap.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet is editorial opinion ('desecrated', 'so that he would be eligible') with no falsifiable factual claim — we can't know Nolan's motivation. The Academy's inclusion standards exist and require 2 of 4 (casting is just one path; crew/leadership/audience also qualify), and Oppenheimer was all-white and won Best Picture under them, so the implied premise is weak — but that's a rebuttal of vibes, not fact-checking. Any note here is a false positive.

fact_check.notes: Academy Inclusion Standards (in effect 2024) require 2/4. Oppenheimer's all-white cast won Best Picture under them. But the tweet is editorial — 'desecrated' is opinion and 'so that he would be eligible' is unverifiable motive.

importance.lens_rationale: 70M-view Elon tweet; cultural-war noise more than misinformation. Suppressing a false-positive note here matters for the notewriter's perceived neutrality.
